title: Netflix Builds Quasar to Measure the Blast Radius of Library API Changes
gist: Netflix built Quasar, an internal tool that indexes symbol definitions/references via SCIP during CI (stored as Parquet in S3, queried with Athena) to show exactly which repositories, dependency versions and call sites a library API change would affect. It complements Revapi and Kythe, is exposed via REST, GraphQL and an MCP server for coding agents, but cannot prove an API is unused because of reflection and incomplete indexing.

themes.theme: Why compatibility checks are not enough

insights.claim: Compatibility tools can flag removed methods or changed signatures but do not identify which applications call them; dependency graphs show declared rather than actual usage, text search misses inheritance/overloads/generated code, and building every consumer is expensive.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Defines a gap in developer tooling (usage-aware impact analysis) that large monorepo/multirepo shops need to fill.

insights.claim: Netflix's Quasar indexes symbol definitions and references using the open SCIP Code Intelligence Protocol, with language-specific indexers submitting data during CI builds, stored in Amazon S3 as Parquet and queried through Amazon Athena.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Shows serverless data-lake stack (S3 + Athena) being reused for code intelligence at scale; validates SCIP as an emerging standard.
insights.locator: Quasar indexes symbol definitions and references

insights.claim: During pull-request analysis Quasar diffs API definitions between commits to find added, removed or modified symbols, then queries indexed references to locate affected repositories, versions and source locations; a Netflix example showed one deprecated-method removal affecting 137 repositories across three library versions.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Quantifies the blast radius of seemingly small library changes in large organisations.
insights.quote: a deprecated method removal affecting 137 repositories across three library versions

insights.claim: Quasar complements Revapi (API compatibility) and Kythe (code navigation); SCIP usage queries cover Java, Go, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript and Rust, while compatibility analysis covers JVM APIs and Protobuf changes traced through generated Java code.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Composable open tooling rather than a monolithic vendor product is how Netflix approaches developer-productivity infrastructure.

insights.claim: An absence of indexed references in Quasar does not prove an API is unused, because reflection, dynamic loading, stale indexes and incomplete coverage can hide consumers.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Static analysis alone cannot safely authorize deletions; expect pairing with runtime telemetry.
insights.locator: However, an absence of indexed references

insights.claim: Knaisoma founder Antonio J. del Aguila noted observed-usage approaches miss reflection and rare-path code such as quarterly batch jobs that may not appear in a sampled window; Netflix's Roberto Perez Alcolea said Netflix is investing in runtime analysis to complement static evidence, without guaranteeing an API is safe to delete.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Hybrid static + runtime impact analysis is the direction for API-lifecycle tooling.
insights.quote: Reflection and incomplete indexing remain blind spots, and we’re also investing in runtime analysis to complement the static evidence.
insights.locator: Antonio J. del Águila, founder of Knaisoma

insights.claim: Netflix exposes Quasar findings through REST, GraphQL and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so both developers and coding agents can consume them.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: MCP is becoming the default integration surface for internal dev tools, expanding demand for agent-readable code intelligence.
insights.locator: Netflix exposes findings through REST, GraphQL

insights.claim: Netflix plans to shift impact analysis earlier into coding workflows so agents identify public API changes and retrieve consumer information before pull requests are opened, preparing migration changes while API and release decisions stay with library producers.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Agent-driven migrations of downstream consumers could cut the cost of library evolution; humans keep governance.
insights.locator: Netflix plans to move impact analysis earlier
